name: arrival-card
title: Arrival Card
description: A square arrival widget: a drawn airliner cruises through a cloud deck that scrolls past behind the landing time.

perf.budget: Each cloud layer is drawn once and then slid as a view on the UI thread, so nothing redraws. The clouds and the sway animate at rest.

measurements.notes: Animating at rest: three cloud layers slide and the plane sways. Holds about 30 fps on this old mid-range phone; Grain Drift measured the same there and Aurora Veil about 10 fps.

a11y.reducedMotion: The plane is in place from the start; it does not fly in or sway, and the clouds stand still.
a11y.screenReader: One label ("KN204. NRT, TOKYO. LANDS AT: 3:25PM. ON SCHEDULE").

meta.guide:
## Usage

```tsx
import { ArrivalCard } from '@/components/kinetik/arrival-card';

<ArrivalCard code="NRT" city="TOKYO" time="3:25PM" status="ON SCHEDULE" tag="KN204" />;
```

## When to use

- A small square widget that answers one question: when does this flight land?
- Next to Route Card and Cruise Dial on a trip screen.

## When not to use

- Lists: each card runs its own cloud shader. Use a plain row.
- Trips that are not by air. The plane is part of the design.

## Notes

- The plane is a vector drawing with no airline's marks. Set `tailColor` and `emblemColor` to your brand colours.
- The plane artwork is credited in `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`.
- The card is square and stops growing at 260 pt.
- The plane flies in once on arrival, then sways gently while the clouds scroll to the left, so it reads as flying forward.

docs: Prefer `npx kinetik-ui add arrival-card`: it installs dependencies with expo install, so versions match your Expo SDK.
